voiceover_script.text: Artificial intelligence is no longer a distant idea. It is already shaping how people learn, communicate, govern and access knowledge.
Across the AI4IA archive, speakers return to a shared question: how can AI expand access to information without deepening existing divides?
The promise of AI is powerful, but the risks are equally real: exclusion, weak infrastructure, language gaps, bias and loss of trust.
The human story is about young people, communities, educators, policymakers and citizens trying to shape technology around real needs.
The archive shows experts connecting AI to governance, rights, media literacy, accessibility, local knowledge and sustainable development.
The way forward is not only better tools. It is inclusive design, local data, ethical governance and public participation.
AI can become a bridge to knowledge, but only if societies choose to build it with transparency, trust and inclusion at the center.
